prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the Labour Party Manifesto 2024 (policy-focused, non-ideological)

Overall approach
- Five missions: sustained economic growth; clean power by 2030; halve serious violent crime; break down barriers to opportunity; build an NHS fit for the future.
- First steps: fiscal stability; 40,000 extra NHS appointments weekly; Border Security Command; Great British Energy; neighbourhood policing measures; 6,500 new teachers.

Economy, tax and business
- Fiscal rules: balance current budget; debt falling by year 5; independent OBR at every fiscal event.
- No increases to National Insurance, basic/higher/additional Income Tax rates, or VAT.
- Close tax loopholes: abolish non-dom status; end offshore trust IHT avoidance; reform carried interest; modernise HMRC to tackle avoidance.
- Industrial Strategy with a statutory council; sector plans (automotive, life sciences, creative, financial services).
- National Wealth Fund £7.3bn to crowd-in private investment: ports, gigafactories, steel, CCS, green hydrogen.
- Business taxation: cap corporation tax at 25% for the parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Infrastructure: 10-year strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; faster planning for nationally significant projects; full gigabit and 5G by 2030.
- Transport: maintain/renew roads; fix 1m potholes annually; EV chargepoint rollout; restore 2030 ICE phase-out; rail brought into public ownership as contracts end; empower bus franchising and municipal ownership.
- Innovation: 10-year R&D budgets; National Data Library; Regulatory Innovation Office; binding rules for developers of the most powerful AI models; ban sexually explicit deepfakes.
- Small business: tackle late payments; easier exporting; procurement access; British Business Bank reform; strengthen Post Office and deliver Horizon justice.

Housing and devolution
- Build 1.5m homes in England: restore mandatory targets; more planners; brownfield-first plus strategic “grey belt” release; new towns; reform compulsory purchase; expand social/affordable homes; protect social stock; first-time buyer priority; permanent mortgage guarantee.
- Devolution: new powers over transport, skills, housing, employment support; multi-year council funding; Local Growth Plans.

Immigration and borders
- Border Security Command with counter-terror-style powers; more caseworkers; returns and enforcement unit; seek new EU security agreement; end hotel use; negotiate returns.
- Reform points-based system; link to domestic skills plans; enforce against employer abuse.

Work, welfare and rights
- Employment support: merge Jobcentre Plus and National Careers Service; youth guarantee (18–21); tackle Access to Work delays; reform/replace Work Capability Assessment.
- Workers’ rights (within 100 days): ban exploitative zero-hours; end fire-and-rehire; day-one rights to sick pay, parental leave, and protection from unfair dismissal; Single Enforcement Body; minimum wage remit to reflect cost of living and remove age bands.

Energy, climate, nature
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen, marine; extend life of existing nuclear; progress Sizewell C and SMRs; maintain gas reserve; no new oil/gas exploration licences; no fracking/coal.
- Great British Energy (publicly owned), capitalised £8.3bn; Local Power Plan; grid upgrades; tougher retail regulation; reduce standing charges.
- Warm Homes Plan: £6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes; PRS efficiency standard by 2030.
- British Jobs Bonus for clean energy supply chains; carbon border adjustment mechanism; restore BoE climate mandate; mandatory net-zero transition plans for major financial firms.
- Nature and water: expand habitats; new National River Walks and Forests; tougher action on sewage; farming: 50% public sector food local/high-standard target; land-use framework; end badger cull; stronger animal welfare measures.

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; new Respect Orders; specific offence for assaulting shopworkers; tighter shoplifting enforcement.
- Knife crime: mandatory Youth Offending Team referral; curfews/tagging; ban zombie/ninja-style blades; online sales enforcement; Young Futures hubs; new offence of criminal exploitation of children.
- Violence against women and girls: specialist units in every force; fast-track rape courts; domestic abuse experts in 999 control rooms; improved stalking and spiking laws.
- Police standards: stronger vetting/misconduct rules; HMICFRS intervention powers; expanded fraud strategy.
- Courts and prisons: more prosecutors; victims’ protections; sentencing review; build prison places; reduce reoffending; probation governance review; address historical injustices (e.g., Hillsborough Law).

Education and families
- Early years: 3,000 school-based nurseries; parental leave review; unique child identifier.
- Schools: 6,500 new teachers; state-school investment funded by ending private school VAT/business rates relief; leadership and inspection reform; curriculum/assessment review; SEND inclusion; school mental health staff; free breakfast clubs in every primary.
- Skills: Skills England; devolve adult skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeship Levy to a Growth and Skills Levy; HE funding reform.
- Culture and sport: creative industries plan; study a creative/vocational subject to 16; ticket resale protections; football regulator.

Health and social care
- NHS: 2m extra operations/scans/appointments a year; shared waiting lists; use independent sector capacity; long-term workforce plan.
- Diagnostics and estates: double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation/adoption strategy; expand clinical trials; enhance NHS app.
- Maternity and safety: more midwives; reduce Black and Asian maternal mortality gap; regulate managers; Royal College of Clinical Leadership; implement Cass Review.
- Primary/community care: more GPs; face-to-face guarantee; modern booking; continuity of care; pharmacist prescribing; optician direct referrals; pilot Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry: 700,000 urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised toothbrushing (ages 3–5).
- Social care: create a National Care Service with national standards; “home first”; Fair Pay Agreement; guaranteed family visiting rights.
- Mental health: 8,500 additional staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act.
- Public health: smoke-free generation; restrict youth-targeted vape marketing; ban junk food ads to children and high-caffeine energy drinks for under-16s; update online safety; gambling reforms; halve healthy life expectancy gap; prioritise women’s health; end new HIV cases by 2030.

Political reform and constitution
- Independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; ban MPs’ paid advisory/consultancy roles; Commons modernisation.
- House of Lords: abolish hereditary peers; mandatory retirement at 80; tougher standards; consult on replacement second chamber.
- Elections: improve voter registration; address voter ID inconsistencies; votes at 16; strengthen donation rules.
- Intergovernmental reset and Council of the Nations and Regions; devolved arrangements for Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland (including implementing the Windsor Framework and replacing the Legacy Act).

Foreign, defence, trade, development
- NATO and nuclear deterrent commitment; Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence; Armed Forces Commissioner; veterans’ visa fee waiver.
- Defence industrial strategy; procurement reform; military strategic HQ; steadfast support for Ukraine and use of frozen Russian assets via allies.
- AUKUS; strategic China approach; protect Overseas Territories’ self-determination.
- EU: improve relationship without rejoining SM/CU/FoM—veterinary deal, MRAs, touring artists, security pact.
- Trade: targeted agreements and sector deals; WTO/CPTPP engagement; India FTA; partnerships with Gulf and Africa; support OECD global minimum tax.
- Climate diplomacy: launch a Clean Power Alliance.
- Development: rebuild capability within FCDO; restore 0.7% GNI when fiscal conditions allow; work with ICAI on value for money.
